messages.text: How do changes in radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Signaling / Non-signaling Tester?

Radar is evolving from standalone sensing toward ISAC, where sensing capability is integrated into communications networks [1].
MFSS may evolve toward joint waveforms such as communications plus radar sensing, or communications methods that provide timing information [3].
This means the measurement target can move from only radar echoes to combined communication-and-sensing waveforms [1][3].
ISAC challenges include high bandwidth, radar equation, power density, spectrum coexistence, and waveform design [1].
Therefore, testers need measurement coverage for wider bandwidth, power-related behavior, coexistence/interference, and waveform quality as radar becomes communication-integrated [1].
Satellite sensing may be active or passive, imaging or non-imaging, and monostatic, bistatic, or multistatic [1].
Automotive radar test configurations already reflect this direction, since AREG-P3 supports monostatic or bistatic frontends, three digital channels, and one object per channel [5].
Therefore, measurement capability must scale from single-channel/single-object testing toward multi-channel and geometry-aware radar scenarios [1][5].
Radar echo generation capability must cover dynamic artificial objects, short-range analog stepped delay for distances below 17 m, fully digital implementation up to 3000 m, and FMCW radar with minimum generated distance equal to the radar-under-test air gap [12].
Advanced radar scenarios also require Doppler control, since each artificial object can support an individual Doppler frequency shift and velocity settings up to ±500 km/h with 0.001 km/h step size when equipped with the cited options [39].
Therefore, required non-signaling radar test capability expands from static RF measurement to dynamic target distance, Doppler, velocity, and FMCW echo simulation [12][39].
For signaling testers, CMX500 supports NR FR1/FR2 signaling and TX measurements, LTE signaling, NB-IoT/NB-NTN signaling, WLAN signaling, fading, AWGN, BLER, CSI report, throughput measurement, and PER measurement [29].
CMX500 also has NR NTN signaling extensions for Rel. 17, Rel. 18, and Rel. 19 [34].
Therefore, as radar becomes integrated with communications and NTN/ISAC concepts, the signaling tester side needs protocol/network-emulation measurements plus RF/TX and channel-condition measurements rather than only RF parametric tests [1][29][34].
For non-signaling testers, CMP200 is described as a 5G NR FR2 nonsignaling one-box test solution for RF parametric testing, pure radiated mmWave setups, mixed radiated/conducted IF setups, and mixed radiated/conducted mmWave setups [26][28].
CMP200 NR FR2 measurements include uplink multi-evaluation results for Modulation, Spectrum, and Power, with settings for 1 to 4 carriers, bands n257/n258/n259/n260/n261/n262, 50/100/200/400 MHz channel bandwidth, 60/120 kHz subcarrier spacing, TDD, and external attenuation [22].
Therefore, non-signaling tester capability needs to cover mmWave RF parametric measurement, radiated and conducted setups, multi-carrier operation, modulation quality, spectrum, and power as communication-side radar-adjacent waveforms become more complex [22][26][28].
【推論】As radar evolves into ISAC and MFSS joint communications-plus-radar waveforms, Signaling Testers need network/protocol emulation with TX, fading, BLER, CSI, throughput, PER, and NTN capability, while Non-signaling Testers need waveform, modulation, spectrum, power, and RF parametric capability [1][3][22][29][34].
【推論】As radar moves toward wider-bandwidth mmWave operation, Non-signaling Testers need higher RF frequency coverage, wider instantaneous bandwidth, IF access, and radiated/conducted mmWave setups [6][7][9][10][28].
【推論】As radar scenarios move from monostatic single-object testing toward bistatic/multistatic and dynamic sensing, testers need multi-channel or multi-antenna support, dynamic artificial-object generation, distance control, Doppler/velocity simulation, and waveform coexistence analysis [1][5][12][39].

passages.text:
6G NTN 展望 › ISAC
[[ISAC]] 將 sensing capability 整合進 communications network。

- satellite sensing 可為 active / passive、imaging / non-imaging、monostatic / bistatic / multistatic。
- ISAC 可能支援 drones、transportation、refrigerated logistics、rural sensing 等 multi-operator collaboration use cases。
- challenge 包含 high bandwidth、radar equation、power density、spectrum coexistence 與 waveform design。

6G NTN 展望 › 3GPP timeline to 6G NTN
來源說：

- 3GPP 於 2023 年 12 月承諾開發 6G specifications。
- Rel. 20 預期啟動 6G use cases / service requirements / technology studies。
- 6G system-level 與 RAN-level technical specifications 預期在 Rel. 21 開始。
- 6G normative phase 預期持續到 2028 年底。
- Timeline 與 [[WRC-27]]、[[WRC-31]]、IMT-2030、Olympic games 2028 / 2030 等外部節點對齊。

6G NTN 展望 › Multi-function satellite services（MFSS）
[[MFSS]] 是將 communications、navigation、earth observation、monitoring、sensing 等 satellite services 整合的概念。

- Phase 1：同一 satellite 整合多個獨立 hardware / services。
- Phase 2：可能整合 joint waveform，例如 communications + radar sensing，或 communications method 提供 timing information。

6G NTN 展望 › Two-stage network access model
來源引述 [[6G-TakeOff]] 提出 UE network access 的 two-stage model：

| Stage | 功能 |
|---|---|
| Anchor part | 提供 downlink synchronization signals、system information、uplink random access；適合 camping、first access、initial connectivity。 |
| Dynamic part | 由 non-permanently visible dynamic cells 組成；較適合 connected mode，UE initial access 後由 network handover 到 dynamic node。 |

此模型的動機是降低 UE 在 idle mode 長時間掃描 dynamic network nodes 的 power consumption。

R&S AREG800A › Automotive radar production configurations
依 [[AREG800A_specs_en_3609-8015-22_v0900]] Version 09.00（September 2025）：

- [[R&S AREG-P1]] radar mini configuration / [[R&S AREG-DBP1]] base unit option：one digital channel，one object per channel，5 GHz instantaneous bandwidth，near object range possibility，analog IF output interfaces，remote control interfaces，[[R&S AREG-MFP]] / [[R&S AREG-BFP]] frontend option one frontend per channel required。
- [[R&S AREG-P2]] radar golden configuration / [[R&S AREG-DBP2]] base unit option：two digital channels。
- [[R&S AREG-P3]] radar pro configuration / [[R&S AREG-DBP3]] base unit option：搭配 [[R&S AREG-MFP]] / [[R&S AREG-BFP]] frontend option；frontend 支援 monostatic 或 bistatic；three digital channels；one object per channel。

R&S AREG800A › R&S AREG8-24S / R&S AREG8-24D
- RF frequency range：`24.0 GHz to 24.25 GHz`。
- RF instantaneous bandwidth：`250 MHz`。
- IF center frequency：`825 MHz for 250 MHz bandwidth`。
- Maximum number supported：`4`；one IF path per [[R&S AREG8-24S]] / [[R&S AREG8-24D]] option required。
- Absolute maximum RX power at frontend：`0 dBm (nom.)`。
- Maximum TX power at frontend：`≥ 15 dBm (meas.)`。
- RF transfer characteristics measurement conditions：with diplexer between RX and TX，frequency step size `2.5 MHz`，measurement bandwidth `1 kHz`，window function normal gate（Hann），type bandpass filter。
- Amplitude flatness：[[R&S AREG8-B9]]，`< ±2 dB in 250 MHz bandwidth (meas.)`。
- Group delay flatness：[[R&S AREG8-B9]]，`< ±1.0 ns in 250 MHz bandwidth (meas.)`。
- Antennas：[[R&S AREG8-24S]] 為 1 combined TX/RX antenna（circulator）；[[R&S AREG8-24D]] 為 1 TX and 1 RX antenna，lateral antenna。
- Antenna type and gain：WR42 rectangular horn antenna。
- Antenna polarization：linear，vertical polarization。
- AUX IF output measurement port：max. `0 dBm`。

Radar is evolving from standalone sensing toward ISAC, where sensing capability is integrated into communications networks [1].
MFSS may evolve toward joint waveforms such as communications plus radar sensing, or communications methods that provide timing information [3].
This means the measurement target can move from only radar echoes to combined communication-and-sensing waveforms [1][3].
ISAC challenges include high bandwidth, radar equation, power density, spectrum coexistence, and waveform design [1].
Therefore, testers need measurement coverage for wider bandwidth, power-related behavior, coexistence/interference, and waveform quality as radar becomes communication-integrated [1].
Satellite sensing may be active or passive, imaging or non-imaging, and monostatic, bistatic, or multistatic [1].
Automotive radar test configurations already reflect this direction, since AREG-P3 supports monostatic or bistatic frontends, three digital channels, and one object per channel [5].
Therefore, measurement capability must scale from single-channel/single-object testing toward multi-channel and geometry-aware radar scenarios [1][5].
Radar echo generation capability must cover dynamic artificial objects, short-range analog stepped delay for distances below 17 m, fully digital implementation up to 3000 m, and FMCW radar with minimum generated distance equal to the radar-under-test air gap [12].
Advanced radar scenarios also require Doppler control, since each artificial object can support an individual Doppler frequency shift and velocity settings up to ±500 km/h with 0.001 km/h step size when equipped with the cited options [39].
Therefore, required non-signaling radar test capability expands from static RF measurement to dynamic target distance, Doppler, velocity, and FMCW echo simulation [12][39].
For signaling testers, CMX500 supports NR FR1/FR2 signaling and TX measurements, LTE signaling, NB-IoT/NB-NTN signaling, WLAN signaling, fading, AWGN, BLER, CSI report, throughput measurement, and PER measurement [29].
CMX500 also has NR NTN signaling extensions for Rel. 17, Rel. 18, and Rel. 19 [34].
Therefore, as radar becomes integrated with communications and NTN/ISAC concepts, the signaling tester side needs protocol/network-emulation measurements plus RF/TX and channel-condition measurements rather than only RF parametric tests [1][29][34].
For non-signaling testers, CMP200 is described as a 5G NR FR2 nonsignaling one-box test solution for RF parametric testing, pure radiated mmWave setups, mixed radiated/conducted IF setups, and mixed radiated/conducted mmWave setups [26][28].
CMP200 NR FR2 measurements include uplink multi-evaluation results for Modulation, Spectrum, and Power, with settings for 1 to 4 carriers, bands n257/n258/n259/n260/n261/n262, 50/100/200/400 MHz channel bandwidth, 60/120 kHz subcarrier spacing, TDD, and external attenuation [22].
Therefore, non-signaling tester capability needs to cover mmWave RF parametric measurement, radiated and conducted setups, multi-carrier operation, modulation quality, spectrum, and power as communication-side radar-adjacent waveforms become more complex [22][26][28].
【推論】As radar evolves into ISAC and MFSS joint communications-plus-radar waveforms, Signaling Testers need network/protocol emulation with TX, fading, BLER, CSI, throughput, PER, and NTN capability, while Non-signaling Testers need waveform, modulation, spectrum, power, and RF parametric capability [1][3][22][29][34].
【推論】As radar moves toward wider-bandwidth mmWave operation, Non-signaling Testers need higher RF frequency coverage, wider instantaneous bandwidth, IF access, and radiated/conducted mmWave setups [6][7][9][10][28].
【推論】As radar scenarios move from monostatic single-object testing toward bistatic/multistatic and dynamic sensing, testers need multi-channel or multi-antenna support, dynamic artificial-object generation, distance control, Doppler/velocity simulation, and waveform coexistence analysis [1][5][12][39].
